cluster_summary: Multiple vulnerabilities arise from deserialization or class loading mechanisms that fail to properly validate the types being instantiated. Attackers can supply arbitrary class names, either through polymorphic deserialization, reflection, or metadata fields, leading to instantiation of dangerous gadgets or unauthorized objects. The predominant pattern involves an incomplete blocklist that misses known dangerous classes, while other cases involve no validation at all or flawed filtering logic.
guideline_text: Trace untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata into deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation. Report code paths where allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 7 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization.

mechanism.missing_guard: allowed classes, object types, and construction side effects are not constrained before deserialization
mechanism.name: untrusted deserialization with attacker-controlled type graph
mechanism.sink_shape: deserializers that instantiate classes, reconstruct object graphs, or invoke callbacks during object creation
mechanism.source_shape: untrusted serialized bytes, object streams, pickles, marshaled payloads, or type metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: use type allowlists, safe codecs, signature checks, or data-only formats instead of general object deserialization

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Extend the blacklist by adding missing dangerous class names, and ideally move to an allowlist approach.
sub_patterns.name: Incomplete blacklist for polymorphic deserialization
sub_patterns.root_cause: The deserialization framework uses a static blacklist of dangerous classes (DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES) that is not exhaustive, allowing attackers to use unlisted gadget classes.
